cards.text: Micah the prophet passes along what the LORD says, and friend, it sounds like a courtroom. Somebody is told to arise and plead a case out loud, and the witnesses being called in aren't even people.

cards.question: The LORD calls on the ___ to hear His case.

cards.text: The mountains are called "you enduring foundations of the earth," and they've been standing there forever. They've seen EVERYTHING, friend. For years, all I saw was the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: True or false: the LORD's case in front of the mountains is against the nations.

cards.text: The LORD has a case against His own people, and He'll argue it against Israel. But the way He opens it? Not how you'd expect.

cards.question: True or false: the LORD opens His case against His people by reading out a list of their sins.

cards.text: He asks a question instead: "My people, what have I done to you? Testify against Me how I have wearied you!" I bet you could hear a crumb drop.

cards.question: Then the LORD reminds His people what He did for them. He brought them up from the land of ___.
Along with Moses, who else does the LORD say He sent before His people?

cards.text: He redeemed them from the house of slavery. Friend, He pulled ME out of a junk drawer, and I tell that story to ANYBODY who stands still for five seconds.
Next, the LORD tells them to remember Balak, king of Moab, and Balaam, son of Beor. Balak sent for Balaam to curse Israel, and Balaam ended up blessing them instead (Numbers 22:5-6; 24:10).
Then He tells them to remember the journey from Shittim to Gilgal. Shittim was where they set out for the Jordan, and Gilgal was where they camped on the other side (Joshua 3:1; 4:19).

cards.question: Why does the LORD want His people to remember Balaam and the journey to Gilgal?

answers.text: So they'll see the LORD has been righteous
So they'll fear the kings around them
So they'll miss their old days in Egypt

cards.text: Now a new voice. Someone asks, "With what shall I come before the LORD when I bow before the God on high?"

cards.question: What's the first gift this person wonders about bringing before the LORD?

answers.text: Gold and silver from the treasury

cards.text: Then the questions get BIGGER: would the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams, or ten thousand rivers of oil? Friend, I tossed one extra scoop of chocolate chips in a batch once and walked around all week like a HERO.

cards.question: True or false: the person even wonders about giving his firstborn for his sin.

cards.text: Then the answer comes, plain and simple: "He has shown you, O man, what is good."

cards.question: So what does the LORD require?

answers.text: Justice and mercy and a humble walk with Him
Bigger offerings brought at every single feast
A long trip up to the temple every year

cards.question: The LORD requires you to act ___, to love ___, and to walk humbly with your God.

findings.problem: The setup line "But the way He opens it? Not how you'd expect." tips the answer to card 6. The expected opening would be a list of sins, so the line tells the baker to pick False.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 10 goes back to the start of Micah 6:4 (redeemed from the house of slavery) after cards 8 and 9 already moved through the rest of that verse to Moses, Aaron and Miriam. It steps backward instead of carrying the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: Card 11 is a flat background note on Balak and Balaam with no Papa Dorin voice. It reads like a study note, not the storyteller.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Card 12 is a flat geography note on Shittim and Gilgal with no Papa Dorin voice. Together with card 11, it makes two voiceless cards in a row.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Card 20 re-asks the content of card 19, whose right answer was "Justice and mercy and a humble walk with Him." The blanks "justly" and "mercy" are already shown, so the card mostly drills the exact wording of Micah 6:8 instead of testing new meaning.
findings.question: Can a fill-in-the-blank card repeat the exact content of the choice card just before it, as a wording follow-up on a key verse? Or should one of the two cards be cut or replaced?
